{{Short description|Mathematics concept}}
In mathematics, a '''Manin triple''' <math>(\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{q})</math> consists of a [[Lie algebra]] ''<math>\mathfrak{g}</math>'' with a non-degenerate invariant [[symmetric bilinear form]], together with two isotropic subalgebras ''<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>'' and ''<math>\mathfrak{q}</math>'' such that ''<math>\mathfrak{g}</math>'' is the direct sum of ''<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>'' and ''<math>\mathfrak{q}</math>'' as a vector space. A closely related concept is the (classical) '''Drinfeld double''', which is an even dimensional Lie algebra which admits a Manin decomposition.

Manin triples were introduced by [[Vladimir Drinfeld]] in 1987, who named them after [[Yuri Manin]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Drinfeld |first1=V. G. |author-link=Vladimir Drinfeld |year=1987 |editor-last=Gleason |editor-first=Andrew |title=Quantum groups |url=https://www.mathunion.org/fileadmin/ICM/Proceedings/ICM1986.1/ICM1986.1.ocr.pdf |journal=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians 1986 |location=Berkeley |publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]] |volume=1 |pages=798–820 |isbn=978-0-8218-0110-9 |mr=934283}}</ref>

In 2001 {{Interlanguage link|Patrick Delorme|lt=Delorme|fr|Patrick Delorme}} classified Manin triples where ''<math>\mathfrak{g}</math>'' is a complex [[reductive Lie algebra]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Delorme |first=Patrick |date=2001-12-01 |title=Classification des triples de Manin pour les algèbres de Lie réductives complexes: Avec un appendice de Guillaume Macey |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0021869301988878 |journal=[[Journal of Algebra]] |volume=246 |issue=1 |pages=97–174 |mr=1872615 |arxiv=math/0003123 |doi=10.1006/jabr.2001.8887 |issn=0021-8693}}</ref>

==Manin triples and Lie bialgebras==
There is an [[equivalence of categories]] between finite-dimensional Manin triples and finite-dimensional Lie bialgebras.

More precisely, if <math>(\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{q})</math> is a finite-dimensional Manin triple, then ''<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>'' can be made into a [[Lie bialgebra]] by letting the [[cocommutator map]] <math>\mathfrak{p} \to \mathfrak{p} \otimes \mathfrak{p}</math> be the dual of the Lie bracket <math>\mathfrak{q} \otimes \mathfrak{q} \to \mathfrak{q}</math> (using the fact that the symmetric bilinear form on ''<math>\mathfrak{g}</math>'' identifies ''<math>\mathfrak{q}</math>'' with the dual of ''<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>''). 

Conversely if ''<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>'' is a Lie bialgebra then one can construct a Manin triple <math>(\mathfrak{p} \oplus \mathfrak{p}^*, \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{p}^*)</math> by letting ''<math>\mathfrak{q}</math>'' be the dual of ''<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>'' and defining the commutator of ''<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>'' and ''<math>\mathfrak{q}</math>'' to make the bilinear form on ''<math>\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{p} \oplus \mathfrak{q}</math>'' invariant.

==Examples==

*Suppose that ''<math>\mathfrak{a}</math>'' is a complex semisimple Lie algebra with invariant symmetric bilinear form ''<math>(\cdot,\cdot)</math>''. Then there is a Manin triple <math>(\mathfrak{g}, \mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{q})</math> with <math>\mathfrak{g} = \mathfrak{a} \oplus \mathfrak{a}</math>, with the scalar product on ''<math>\mathfrak{g}</math>'' given by ''<math>( (w,x),(y,z) ) = (w,y) - (x,z)</math>''. The subalgebra ''<math>\mathfrak{p}</math>'' is the space of diagonal elements ''<math>(x,x)</math>'', and the subalgebra ''<math>\mathfrak{q}</math>'' is the space of elements ''<math>(x,y)</math>'' with ''<math>x</math>'' in a fixed [[Borel subalgebra]] containing a Cartan subalgebra ''<math>\mathfrak{h}</math>'', ''<math>y</math>'' in the opposite Borel subalgebra, and where ''<math>x</math>'' and ''<math>y</math>'' have the same component in ''<math>\mathfrak{h}</math>''.
